incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) – Articles L.227-1 through L.227-4, L.123-1, L.123-9, R.227-1, R.123-104, and applicable provisions of Title II of Book I (registered companies).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), ultimately leading to recording in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier de formalité unique de création d'entreprise : Statuts d'une Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) and Formulaire d'immatriculation M0 (Déclaration de création d'une personne morale) submitted electronically through the Guichet Unique.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SAS; shareholders may set a freely determined amount in the Articles. If any capital is subscribed, full payment for shares represented by in-kind contributions or at least 50% of nominal cash shares must be made at subscription and deposited with a regulated French financial institution or a notary as a sequestration act until the RCS registration. Release of capital occurs after registration and issuance of the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, pursuant to French law, that the shareholders of the Société par Actions Simplifiée hereby (i) adopt the Articles of Association of the Company as presented; (ii) subscribe, for a consideration stated in the Articles, and fully authorize the payment of the initial share capital; (iii) approve the escrow deposit of such capital in accordance with legal rules; (iv) adopt the registered office address designated in the Articles and authorize the Chairman to enter into a lease and the relevant administrative declarations; (v) appoint the natural person acting as Président and any Directeur Général; and (vi) grant full powers to the Chairman to complete the RCS filing, publish the legal announcement, obtain the Kbis extract, and undertake all ancillary formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the SAS Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (option) or private deed; articles filed electronically with the Guichet Unique / INPI; mandatory prior to RCS filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Declare in writing the corporate form, company name, duration, registered office, share capital, share distribution, management powers, decision-making procedures, collective decision rights, and legal representative. If any capital is due, issue a declaration that the funds have been paid. Have each shareholder sign the articles, acknowledging the subscriptions. Where a notary is used, obtain notarized original or an authentic copy.
required_dossiers: Signed original or authentic copy of the Articles of Association
Non-conviction declaration (certificat de non-condamnation) of the legal representative
Identity documents of each shareholder and the legal representative
Bank certificate of capital deposit (attestation de blocage des fonds) or notary attestation
Proof of availability and lawful use of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique rejects the filing as incomplete or formally defective, the applicant receives an editorial notification; cure defects by uploading supplementary documents or a correcting attachment to the electronic file within 15 days without losing the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a legal announcement of incorporation in a journal d'annonces légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A newspaper authorized to receive legal announcements (Support d'annonces légales) in the judicial district of the proposed registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office address, corporate purpose, intended RCS jurisdiction / court name, and legal representative details. Verify the announcement text in the local authorized press release and obtain the proof of publication (justificatif de parution). For SAS with duly appointed management, announcement publication is required prior to or concurrently with filing through the Guichet Unique.
required_dossiers: Proposed text of the legal announcement
Corporate identification (name, SAS, registered office, capital, duration)
Identity of legal representative
Request copy of the adjudication / invoice from the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL queries content corrections (e.g., incomplete corporate purpose or capital disclosure), amend the notice and re-submit to the same publication; the RCS filing will not be refused by the court solely due to a minor announcement defect where the applicant provides a corrective annexed public notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit statutory documents and apply for RCS registration via the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (INPI) under the delegated authority of the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the Guichet Unique portal, select the ‘Création d’entreprise’ procedure, choose ‘Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS)’, and complete the M0 registration form. Attach electronically signed copies of the Articles, legal announcement justification, capital deposit certificate, identity documents, non-conviction declarations, and proof of registered office occupancy. Confirm the legal representatives and regulated agent (if any). Pay the official filing fee electronically.
required_dossiers: Form M0 (complete electronic declaration)
Verbatim copy of the Articles of Association
Proof of publication in a JAL
Certificate of deposit of capital (attestation de consignation)
Copy of identity document of the legal representative
Non-conviction declaration of the legal representative
Lease agreement, ownership deed, or free occupancy letter for the registered office
Electronically signed information sheet (controlling person declaration where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique issues a ‘complétude’ (incompleteness) query, provide the requested documents through the portal within 15 days; if the registry refuses registration, rectify the file and, if necessary, request a ruling from the presiding judge of the commercial court (Tribunal de commerce) under Articles R.123-104 et seq. of the Commercial Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive RCS registration, Kbis extract, and update tax and social declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; the Kbis extract is the official corporate identity and authentication document.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful examination by the registry, verify that the Kbis extract accurately reflects the corporate name, registered office, legal form, capital, legal representatives, and ISIC activity code. Require a certified copy of the Kbis as official proof of incorporation. Register the corporate identity with the French tax administration (DGFiP) and the social administration (Urssaf) via the Guichet Unique. Retain the registration number (SIREN) and the taxpayer identification number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) obtained from the relevant authorities.
required_dossiers: Valid Kbis extract
SIREN / SIRET number notification
TVA intracommunautary number confirmation (if applicable)
Affiliation preferences and workplace registration (Urssaf), business insurance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis refuses to reflect an activity change or contains a data error, a correction request (demande de rectification) must be addressed to the greffe with the underlying statutory proof; the judge of liberty of the commercial court may be seized if the correction is not effected within a reasonable period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Préfecture de police (for certain office premises) and the Direction Départementale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) for commercial activity declarations; for software / SaaS operations, no industrial manufacturing license is required under the French classification of activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration of the place of business and, when applicable, a déclaration préalable or attestation de sécurité for premises open to the public. For pure software AIGC activity, no specific trade license is needed; the company must hold an ‘activity declaration’ through the Guichet Unique for social and tax affiliation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), within the Ministry responsible for the ecological transition.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA required for purely administrative / digital service activity confined to an office environment without manufacturing, effluent discharge, or hazardous substance storage. The activity falls outside the RIIEPM (Rubriques de la nomenclature des installations classées) thresholds and the automatic EIA category.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with general French environmental obligations for operators of office-based activities: strict management of electrical and electronic waste (DEEE) under the European Waste Directive (2012/19/EU), obligation to prevent wastewater overload in building discharge, and compliance with in-door noise limits under the French Public Health Code (art. R.1334-33). For data-center servers, if any, meet the thresholds of the Energy Transition Law (capacité électrique), monitor heat emissions, and apply the best available energy efficiency techniques.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For offices staffed with employees, the premises must comply with the French Labor Code (Code du travail – articles R.4222-1 onwards): indoor air volume, natural lighting, temperature control, electrical and fire safety, accessible emergency exits, and first aid equipment. A building permit (permis de construire) or prior administrative authorization (déclaration préalable) is required if any structural modifications are made to the rented space. Fire safety certification (attestation de sécurité) is required when premises are open to the public or where the local fire brigade (Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours – SDIS) undertakes a technical inspection. The employer must also file a ‘accident du travail’ registration with URSSAF/CARSAT and obtain an occupational health and safety statement; for a SaaS or AI video-generation activity the workplace risk assessment (document unique) must list technical and cyber-risks, and the company must maintain a compliance checklist for electrical equipment and workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Ministry of Economy and Finance; professional online portal: impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel); single business formalities portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; VAT administration governed by the Code Général des Impôts (CGI); customs administration (exports, EORI) is supervised by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI), portal: douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned SAS obtains statutory tax identifiers as follows: (1) file incorporation and initial disclosures electronically on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (single national portal effective 1 January 2023); (2) INSEE issues the SIREN (9-digit) and SIRET (14-digit) identifiers and notifies DGFiP, creating the enterprise's tax file; (3) DGFiP assigns the French intra-community VAT number in the format FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN under art. 286 ter CGI, together with the corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) account reference; (4) for immediate VAT invoicing, complete electronic registration through the professional portal (demande d'immatriculation, equivalent to form 3527-SD); (5) for export activity, separately obtain an EORI number (FR + SIREN) from DGDDI; (6) where the taxable person is a non-established foreign entity supplying B2C digital services into France, a fiscal representative may be mandatory (art. 286-1 al. 4 CGI) and registration is effected through the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) with DGFiP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no check-the-box regime: an SAS has a fixed legal status and is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax (art. 206-1 CGI). Available statutory elections: (i) art. 239 bis AB CGI — newly created small companies (turnover ≤ €10m in the first fiscal year and qualifying shareholders) may elect, for the first five fiscal years, taxation at the shareholder level (pass-through treatment); (ii) art. 223 A CGI — group tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) for a French parent holding at least 95% of French subsidiaries, elected at the opening of a fiscal year; (iii) art. 145 CGI — parent-subsidiary régime mère-fille 95% exemption on qualifying dividends with 5% recapture; (iv) the French anti-hybrid rules (transposing ATAD 1 and 2) under arts. 212 bis and 205 ter CGI neutralize hybrid mismatch outcomes and provide no elective reclassification for an SAS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) — French Value Added Tax (VAT), transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; administered under arts. 256 to 260 CGI and CGI Annexe II/III; distinct from the US sales-and-use-tax model.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registrational threshold for persons established in France: any person performing an independent economic activity with a French nexus must register for VAT from the first euro of turnover (déclaration dès le premier euro). The only statutory exemption is the franchise en base de TVA (art. 293 B CGI) for qualifying established small enterprises whose annual turnover is ≤ €91,900 for supplies of goods and ≤ €47,500 for services (2025 revalorised scale); during the franchise the business is exempt from charging VAT and from filing VAT returns, though optional registration remains permitted. Non-established foreign suppliers of electronically supplied services (including AI avatar video generation SaaS) must register via the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) or French VAT number to account for B2C French VAT from the first euro, with no threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting reform enacted by art. 921 of the Loi de finances pour 2024 and implemented by decree (notably décret n° 2024-1523 of 27 December 2024): from 1 September 2026, all French VAT-registered businesses must receive structured electronic invoices, and large enterprises plus mid-tier companies (ETI) must issue them through a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP — Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the State-run Public Invoicing Portal (PPF — Portail Public de Facturation); from 1 September 2027, SMEs and micro-enterprises must also issue e-invoices. Transmission is API-based using standard formats (Factur-X, UBL, EDI) with mandatory transaction and payment data reporting to DGFiP on the same timetable. France does not apply fiscal digital stamping or real-time clearance; penalties apply under art. 1734 CGI (€15 per non-compliant invoice, capped at €15,000 per calendar year) together with administrative fines for failure to transmit e-reporting data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to destinations outside the EU are exempt from French VAT with full credit for input VAT (effective 0%) under art. 262-I CGI, provided the goods physically leave EU territory as evidenced by the electronic Customs Export Declaration (DAU) processed in the DGDDI DELTA system. Intra-EU supplies (livraisons intracommunautaires) qualify for the corresponding exemption under art. 262 ter CGI where the customer holds a valid EU VAT number and the goods are dispatched to another Member State (EC Sales List filing). For AI avatar video generation software supplied as an electronically supplied service: B2B supplies are outside French VAT when the recipient is established outside France (place-of-supply rule, art. 259 CGI); B2C supplies to French consumers are subject to French VAT at 20%; B2C supplies to consumers in other EU Member States are declared via the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) at the destination state's rate; B2C supplies to non-EU customers are outside the scope of French VAT and follow local consumption rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU / Document Administratif Unique submitted electronically via DELTA through the National Single Window) cleared and discharged by DGDDI showing the exporting SAS as declarant/exporter
Transport document evidencing physical exit from the EU: Bill of Lading (Connaissement) for sea carriage, CMR consignment note for road freight, or Air Waybill for air carriage
Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of delivery/arrival in the non-EU destination (or the destination country's customs entry document)
Inward Remittance Certificate: SWIFT MT103 or bank statement evidencing payment of the export proceeds into the French exporter's bank account

For intra-EU zero-rated supplies: customer's valid intra-community VAT number, the EC Sales List (état récapitulatif des clients) and, where thresholds apply, the monthly/quarterly Intrastat DEB (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under art. 283 CGI and DGFiP doctrine (BOI-TVA-CHAMP-40-10), the exporter bears the burden of proving the physical export; missing or inconsistent documentation triggers reassessment of French VAT at 20% plus monthly late interest (0.20% per month), within the standard three-year statute of limitation (art. L. 176 LPF), extended where fraud is alleged. Penalties follow art. 1729 CGI: 40% for bad faith (mauvaise foi) and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (manœuvres frauduleuses) or abuse of right. Fraudulent zero-rating or fictitious exports further expose the SAS and its directors to criminal tax fraud under art. 1741 CGI (fine up to €500,000 and up to five years' imprisonment, with aggravated amounts doubled), to clawback of deducted input VAT (art. 272 CGI), and to solidary liability where the issuer knew the transaction was irregular; e-invoicing and e-reporting failures attract the specific fines of art. 1734 CGI (€15 per invoice, capped at €15,000 per year).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) — member of the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); banking and market-infrastructure supervision delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); foreign-exchange statistical reporting, balance-of-payments surveillance, and external financial relations policy coordinated with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under a fully liberalised convertibility regime for both current and capital account items, consistent with Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (free movement of capital), EU Capital Markets Union rules, and the OECD Codes of Liberalisation. There are no exchange-control licensing, prior dividend-remittance authorisation, foreign-currency quota, or profit-blocking mechanisms applicable to a French SAS. Profits may be remitted freely to non-resident shareholders, subject to (i) corporate-law tests under Articles L. 232-11 to L. 232-18 of the Code de commerce (no distribution of net assets below share capital), (ii) French withholding tax under Article 119 bis of the Code général des impôts (CGI) at the domestic 25% rate, reduced to 0% for qualifying EEA corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) where at least 10% ownership and the applicable holding period are satisfied, and reduced further under bilateral treaties (e.g., 15% standard on dividends under most OECD treaties, with lower 5% portfolio thresholds where available), and (iii) CRS/FATCA reporting obligations which do not constrain the remittance itself. Convertibility is real and immediate: the Banque de France publishes daily euro reference rates, and repurchase of EUR is unlimited. The only functional constraints arise from EU/UN/OFAC sanctions screening, anti-money-laundering origin-of-funds diligence, and the general prohibition on financing sanctioned persons — none of which amounts to a currency-convertibility hurdle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is expressly no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion of foreign currency export receipts into EUR, and no compulsory repatriation timeline in France. The regime is governed by the Code monétaire et financier (Articles L. 151-1 to L. 165-1), which abolished exchange controls and replaced them with statistical and AML reporting obligations. A French AI/software exporter may invoice in USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, or any agreed currency, hold export receipts in foreign-currency accounts with authorised credit institutions, and choose commercially rational conversion timing. The mandatory framework consists of (i) bank-filed balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque de France for every cross-border payment equal to or above EUR 15,000, with bank-assigned transaction and purpose codes; (ii) continued retention of underlying contracts, invoice files, commercial documentation, and, for exports outside the EU, customs export declarations (exit summaries via the DELTA declaration system), while intra-EU sales require Intrastat/Recapitulative statement reporting where thresholds apply; (iii) compliance with EU Regulation 2015/847 (information accompanying funds transfers) for payable-through and correspondent chains; and (iv) arm's-length transfer pricing documentation for any intercompany settlement in accordance with Article 57 CGI and the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines. No conversion ratio or exchange-surrender timetable is imposed by Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_repatriation_and_dividend_remitt: In addition to the above, there is no requirement to obtain a French Treasury clearing order for dividend or capital distributions. Capital reduction distributions and total or partial liquidation proceeds are freely transferable through authorised banks, provided the distributable reserve and solvency tests are met and the bank records the underlying documentation. Where the receiving shareholder is resident in a country listed on the French counter-tax-haven blacklist (États non coopératifs), a 75% withholding may apply under Article 238-0 A CGI; treaty-relief procedures (reduced withholding at source or refund procedure) remain available.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte de consignation / compte d'apport) and multi-currency Operational Account (EUR, USD, GBP)
Operational EUR and USD account with dedicated SG corporate international desk; secondary escrow account for capital injections

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Domestic ACPR-licensed French fintech banks and electronic-money institutions (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Allicance? Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for operational liquidity, LOW-MEDIUM for escrow and hedging. Such providers offer rapid remote onboarding, multi-currency IBANs, virtual cards, and automated accounting feeds, making them viable as an ancillary operating account for collection of Stripe/Paddle payouts, but they are not licensed credit institutions and therefore cannot hold client funds as true deposits, issue commercial letters of credit, provide authorised lending, furnish derivative documentation, or ensure protected custody of statutory share capital. Cross-border offshore digital EMIs: a UK FCA-authorised EMI cannot passport into France post-Brexit; it requires either a separate French ACPR licence under the PSD2 regime, a French branch, or reliance on the limited reverse-solicitation exemption, and any UK-handled collection will be regarded by French banks as a non-regulated payment intermediary — an AML concentration risk. EEA-licensed EMIs (e.g., Lithuanian, Dutch, Irish, German) may passport into France through freedom to provide services or a branch, but in practice Tier-1 French banks will require that the final settlement of material outbound flows (royalties, dividends, intercompany invoices, supplier payments above EUR 50,000) pass through a fully supervised French credit institution rather than an EMI cascading structure. Overall viability: use a regulated French fintech (e.g., Qonto) for day-to-day operational collection and expense management in parallel with a Tier-1 universal bank for statutory capital, escrow, clearing, and hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the Tier-1 universal banks listed above, physical attendance of the SAS's authorised legal representative (the Président or a formally appointed mandataire with corporate power under the SAS internal articles) at a French branch or the bank's corporate international desk is de facto mandatory for the initial due-diligence interview, identity verification, signature validation, and activation of signing mandates. Certain relationship desks permit fully remote onboarding where the entity is introduced by a reputable international law firm or notary; otherwise, a French-resident corporate officer or an appointed proxy may attend with a notarised power of attorney. Remote opening is standard for ACPR-regulated French fintech/EMI providers, using video identification in accordance with Article R. 561-5-1 and Article R. 561-5-2 of the Code monétaire et financier, supplemented by a valid Kbis extract showing registered ownership and the beneficial-owner declaration, LEI number (where required for securities or derivatives), proof of substance (lease agreement, utility invoice, payroll evidence), and company bank references. Non-resident directors are not per se excluded; they are instead subjected to enhanced due diligence: sanctioned-jurisdiction screening, source-of-wealth documentation, physical passport authentication with apostille/legalisation, and a UBO certificate. The practical recommendation is to appoint a Paris-based local director (or proxy) for the onboarding interview while keeping the foreign beneficial owners disclosed, and to present the rundown: RCS/Kbis, articles of incorporation (statuts), UBO form, shareholder register (registre des titres), proof of AI software commercial traction (Stripe/Paddle dashboard), and a source-of-funds letter for the initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership arising from a multi-layered foreign parent / managed fund holding the French SAS shares and control rights.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original RCS extract (extrait Kbis) issued within 3 months and evidencing the filed beneficial-owner declaration; full ownership org chart down to natural persons holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of the SAS share capital or voting rights; certified passport copies plus proof of address for each ultimate beneficial owner; current self-certification of UBO in the bank's prescribed form; formation certificate of the immediate parent with apostille and legalised translation, and, where the shareholder is itself a fund or SPV, a fund constitutional summary, capitalisation table, and regulatory identification (e.g., AIFM/RAIF/managed fund registration).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse-media flags triggered by shareholders, directors, counterparties, or customers located in high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Russia, Belarus, Iran) via the AI SaaS global distribution model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions-screening reports (EU/UN/OFAC/HM Treasury lists) covering all directors, UBOs, signatories, major customers, and banking counterparties; geolocation and IP-subnet blocking policy excluding sanctioned countries from the AI video-generation platform; dual-use export-control classification opinion under EU Regulation 2021/821 confirming the software is not an enumerated dual-use item requiring authorisation; customer lists from Stripe/Paddle in readable format; and an internal AML/CTF policy manual subscribed by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue velocity and typography mismatch: a newly incorporated SAS, low capital, recently opened account, yet immediately receiving high volumes of USD subscription payments attributed to AI-generated avatar video products without visible French operating substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed SaaS master agreements, order forms, and terms-of-service for the ten largest customers; historical payment ledgers exported from Stripe and Paddle showing subscriber counts, ARPU, churn, chargebacks, and settlement cycles; evidence of compute and storage infrastructure contracts (cloud provider invoices, model-hosting agreements); payroll and contractor agreements demonstrating French development and compliance headcount; invoicing template used for B2B licences; transfer-pricing documentation for any intercompany licensing fee; and an explanatory memorandum on the precise AIGC functionality (text-to-video, avatar generation, digital-human licensing) to satisfy the bank's commercial understanding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a non-resident investor or venture fund without clear economic rationale or documented source of wealth, particularly amounts above EUR 500,000.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial or counsel-certified deed of capital subscription (acte de souscription d'actions) recording the share premium and the exact amount; resolution of the SAS's shareholders or the sole shareholder approving the capital increase and the post-transaction shareholding structure; bank reference letter (less than 3 months old) from the investor's primary bank; audited or banker-certified financial statements of the subscribing entity; a letter of explanation of the funding source (e.g., realisation of prior exits, operation profit, fund commitments); and confirmation that the increase will be registered with the RCS within the 1-month legal window.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound payments to non-EU content-production, marketing, or freelancer networks inconsistent with the board-declared SaaS business model, risking misclassification of services or transfer-pricing challenges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed service agreements and deliverables documentation; substantiated invoices with attributable project milestones; proof of the payee's legal substance (company register extract, VAT/GST certificate); payroll/external-contractor policy; board minutes authorising the relevant expense category; beneficial-owner declaration of each significant supplier; and a transaction-pattern explanation that the dedicated operational account is cordoned from the capital escrow account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol for capital contributions into the French SAS: the foreign shareholder or investor shall transfer funds in EUR (or convertible currency) via SWIFT MT103 from a fully-disclosed originating account directly to the SAS's IBAN at the Tier-1 French bank, with field 50K identifying the immediate payer, field 59 identifying the SAS, and the remittance narrative expressly stating 'Apport en capital / capital subscription to FR_SAS', including the reference of the notarised deed or shareholder resolution and the date of the corporate act. ISO 20022 purpose-code mapping: since there is no universally valid ISO purpose code for pure equity injection, the practical practice is to combine narrative phrase 'Apport en capital — augmentation de capital — prime d'émission' with the French balance-of-payments statistical category 'Direct Investment — Equity/Quasi-equity' assigned by the receiving bank; where intra-group funding is used for working capital, the ISO purpose code 'INTC' (intra-company payment) is commonly accepted; for royalties/licences subsequent to subscription use 'ROYA' and for dividends use 'DIVI'. Verification requirements: (i) the bank will perform sanctions screening against EU/UN/OFAC lists; (ii) for amounts at or above EUR 15,000 the bank must log the transfer with the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics; (iii) the SAS must ensure the share capital increase is legally effective before or within the 1-month RCS filing window and provide the updated Kbis to the bank within the prescribed post-closing period; (iv) for injections above EUR 500,000, the bank may require the full source-of-funds dossier (shareholder financial statements, deed, bank reference letter, UBO certificate) before final crediting; and (v) if the funds arrive in USD, the receiving bank will convert at a commercial rate or a pre-agreed spot forward rate, and the SAS should request two-day value dating and a confirmation of the applied FX rate. No prior Banque de France authorisation is required, and the transfer is not subject to any domestic capital surcharge or confirmation by the Ministry of Economy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing and disbursement rails for the French SAS: (i) for payments to EEA/SEPA counterparties in EUR — use SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) via XML pain.001, requiring the payee's IBAN, which clears through T2 (TARGET2) infrastructure via Banque de France and is credited within one business day; (ii) for cross-border USD and non-EUR payments — use SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfer, with field 33B indicating currency and amount, field 56C/57A advising the intermediary institution, field 59 the ultimate beneficiary, and narrative containing the invoice/reference number; USD transfers settle via correspondent banks (typically JPMorgan, Citi, or Bank of New York Mellon for French banks) across Fedwire/CHIPS; (iii) where a foreign buyer requires documentary payment security for software deliverables or a trade financing structure, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) may be opened by the buyer's issuing bank and confirmed by the French confirming bank, available at sight with documents stipulated; subsequent reimbursement is executed through SWIFT MT202/MT103 between banks; (iv) for SaaS subscription collection from Stripe and Paddle — these flows arrive as card-not-present commercial settlements (scheme money) into the merchant settlement account of the payment processor and are then swept to the SAS's operational cluster; such flows do not travel over SWIFT and must be reconciled using processor settlement reports and platform payout statements, with the SAS maintaining a cash-application procedure against a receivable sub-ledger (e.g., 28-day DSO tracking); (v) for outbound dividend and royalty remittances to foreign shareholders — use SWIFT MT103 with purpose narrative 'DIVIDEND' or 'ROYALTY', attach the applicable withholding-tax computation and, where treaty relief is claimed, the approved reduced-withholding certificate or refund dossier; the bank will screen against EU Regulation 2015/847 and French AML legislation, including the mandatory collection of payee UBO data for payees that are legal persons; (vi) USD cheques are not recommended in France, and intra-EU invoices above commercial thresholds are normally settled by SEPA direct debit or SEPA CT rather than MT103 to reduce cost and optical character recognition risk? While keeping the narrative concise, the treasury should pre-agree cut-off times (typically 13:00 CET for same-day EUR, 12:00 CET for USD) and should maintain a dedicated operational account strictly separated from the capital escrow account to simplify audit trails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX transactions (comptant) for same-day/T+2 settlement of USD, GBP, JPY receivable into EUR
Outright deliverable FX forwards (change à terme ferme) up to 24 months for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and EUR/CNY exposures
FX swaps (swap de change) for short-dated liquidity and rolled-forward hedging of recurring USD revenue

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or restricted currencies of trading counterparties (e.g., INR, KRW, TWD, ARS), documented under an ISDA 1998 Master Agreement with fallback twelve/twenty-location spot fixing
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (XCCY IRS) under ISDA/CSA for hedging long-dated USD-denominated subscription-price indices or intercompany loan exposure to the EUR balance sheet

Vanilla FX options (call/spread and put strategies) for contingent USD/EUR conversion and tender-related exposure, traded with the Tier-1 bank's market desk and requiring an ISDA/CSA credit support annex or a collateral deposit
Average-rate (Asian) forward contracts for smoothing USD subscription-income conversion across monthly settlement cycles

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements (Comptes Annuels) with RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) under the Ministry of the Economy, Industry and the Digital Economy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 6 months after the closing of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 1,500 EUR and potential dissolution proceedings after prolonged delay

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Corporate Income Tax Return (Déclaration de l'Impôt sur les Sociétés - IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Authorities (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques - DGFiP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.2% per month of tax due, interest charges, and possible tax reassessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Update of Beneficial Owners (Bénéficiaires Effectifs) to RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Upon any change in ownership or control; annual confirmation recommended if no changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 1,500 EUR and potential administrative sanctions for non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit required if the SAS meets at least two of the following criteria: annual turnover exceeding 800,000 EUR, total assets exceeding 400,000 EUR, or average number of employees exceeding 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (PCG - Plan Comptable Général)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership details to the RCS; updates mandatory within one month of any shareholding transfer or change in control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 8,000-25,000 USD depending on company size and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) under article 219-I-CGI; reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 38,120 of annual taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% of capital held directly or indirectly by natural persons.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above that cap; Young Innovative Company (JEI) status grants partial IS exemption (30% or 60% of profit depending on company age, capped at EUR 100,000 per year) for companies with R&D intensity above 15%, incorporated within the last 11 years, unlisted, and with less than 50 employees; tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) permits single payment of IS by the head of a French group. Loss carryforward is unlimited in duration under article 209-I-CGI but, for large enterprises, the annual deduction is capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding that threshold; a fiscal-year carryback (option pour le report en arrière) is limited to EUR 1,000,000 and is refundable over a five-year period. Non-resident corporations holding a French SAS are taxable in France only through a French permanent establishment for business profits; the SAS itself is always resident in France.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n° 2065-SD (Cerfa n° 15939) together with annexed schedules 2058-A to 2058-XX; mandatory electronic filing via impots.gouv.fr professional portal (Espace Professionnel / EDI-EFI) under the DGFiP PGD exchange format. Paper filing is not permitted for companies subject to corporate income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual liquidation return, supplemented by four quarterly prepayment instalments (acomptes) due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December; the annual return reconciles the prepayments and shows the final balance (solde) payable with the filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual IS return must be filed within three months of the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year entity (financial year ending 31 December), the deadline is the third business day of May; e.g., for FY 2023 the deadline was 3 May 2024. For a non-calendar year-end, the deadline is the final day of the third month following the closing date (e.g., 30 June for a 31 March year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit (bénéfice imposable) subject to the standard 25% rate, computed from net accounting income after adjustments on annexes 2058-A and 2058-B.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SAS is owned entirely by non-residents, the entity remains fully French-resident and must file the return covering worldwide results unless a permanent establishment outside France is separately taxed; report French-source trading profit and all French PE-attributable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit eligible for the reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 38,120 tranche.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only available where the French entity itself satisfies the SME statutory tests (turnover below EUR 10 million, 75% natural-person ownership, capital fully paid up); non-resident corporate shareholders therefore disqualify the reduced rate unless they are transparent interposed entities holding all shares and the beneficial-ownership condition is met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends and participation receipts benefiting from the 95% parent-subsidiary exemption (régime mère-fille).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the relevant annex (2058-AA); the 5% quota of non-deductible expenses is added back; for a French SAS receiving dividends from a subsidiary abroad, the 2-year holding-period minimum is satisfied by an undertaking on the return; foreign-source withholding taxes remain creditable or deductible only under treaty-specific provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annex 2058-B, Section 'Résultat fiscal avant imputation des déficits'
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between accounting profit/loss and taxable income, including deductions for R&D tax credit, innovation tax credit, and exceptional provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot cause the French entity to deduct head-office charges unless a full cost-sharing analysis is maintained; intra-group recharge invoices must be evidenced by a documented transfer pricing policy.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Carried-forward tax losses applied against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The deduction is limited to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit above that amount where prior-year losses exceed EUR 1,000,000; a reconciliation schedule of each loss year must be attached; failure to maintain the loss register leads to automatic disallowance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% automatic surcharge (majoration) when the return is filed more than 30 days after a formal notice, then an additional 5% per month or part of a month, capped at 40%; late-payment interest (intérêts de retard) accrues at 0.20% per month from the original due date. Absence of any return allows tax assessment ex officio (taxation d'office) with the 40% penalty and interest; where fraud is proved, the 80% penalty applies. Directors face personal collection under article L.267-LPF for penalties resulting from misconduct.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory withholding of 25% on dividends distributed by a French SAS to non-resident corporate shareholders (article 119 bis (2) CGI); 12.8% final withholding (PFU) for non-resident natural persons. Distributions to a qualifying EU/EEA parent under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive are exempt from French withholding where the parent holds at least 10% of the capital, has held it for at least 2 years, meets the anti-abuse and substance requirements, and the parties are eligible corporate forms within the directive. French-resident corporate shareholders receive dividends without withholding and may apply the 95% participation exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double taxation agreement (DTA), the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the French paying entity, before the payment date, with a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by its State of residence and a completed declaration (Form 5000 or the treaty-specific specific form) establishing beneficial ownership and absence of a French permanent establishment connected to the shares. Where withholding has already been applied, the creditor must file a refund claim (Form 5001 or a pro-forma claim) with the DGFiP Service des Impôts des Entreprises no later than 31 December of the second calendar year following the year in which the withholding was levied. Under the EU Directive, the parent company must deliver a Form 5003 (attestation mère-fille) stating that it is subject to corporate tax in its State of residence without an option for exemption and confirming the 10% / 2-year holding conditions; the French payer must keep such evidence to withstand reassessment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and patent/licence fees: statutory French withholding of 33.33% (art. 125 and 1678 CGI for industrial-property rights and copyright) unless reduced by an applicable DTA (commonly 0-10%, e.g., France-United States: 10% on patents, 0% on pure copyright royalties; France-United Kingdom: 10% on most industrial royalties; France-China: 10%). Software payments must be carefully characterised between copyright rights (royalty) and supply of services (no withholding). Interest: statutory 0% withholding for arm's length debt interest paid to EU/EEA residents or residents of treaty States with an administrative assistance agreement; a punitive 75% withholding applies to interest paid to entities located in non-cooperative States or territories (NCG) under article 238-0 A-CGI, unless beneficial ownership and substance can be demonstrated.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory preparation of the French Master File and Local File arises where either (i) the French entity's annual turnover exceeds EUR 50 million, or (ii) the worldwide group's consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 750 million (article L. 13 AA-LPF). Entities below these thresholds must nevertheless keep and, upon formal demand, produce documentation demonstrating that intercompany prices for AI video-generation services, hosting, GPU capacity, software licences, SaaS subscriptions, and group services are consistent with the arm's length principle. Failure to furnish complete documentation on request triggers a penalty of 5% of the gross amount of the undocumented cross-border intra-group transactions (article 1735 ter-CGI), in addition to any adjustment and late-payment interest.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a dedicated Economic Substance Regulation statute akin to the UAE/offshore ESR regime; however, treaty benefits and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive require genuine economic substance in the State of residence (real decision-making, personnel, premises, and business activity). Artificial arrangements lacking substance are recharacterised under the French abuse-of-law doctrine (article L. 64-LPF) and the OECD BEPS GAAR, causing denial of treaty relief, reclassification of the French SAS as fiscally transparent, and an 80% penalty. The AI avatar video SaaS entity must therefore demonstrate real operational substance in France (engineering team, servers or cloud contracts negotiated from France, strategic meetings, IP ownership and payroll) to protect its DTA position.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission or understatement of taxable revenue on the 2065-SD return, including deliberate non-declaration of SaaS subscription income, fabricated deductions, offshore artificial profit shifting, or false invoices for AI compute capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741-CGI: 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 500,000, increased to twice the illicit proceeds when the offence is committed as an organised group or using an overseas conduit; complementary penalties may include publication of the conviction, closure of the business, and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative (Président / Directeur Général) is prosecuted as perpetrator or accomplice; courts may impose a travel ban, suspension of civic rights, a prohibition on managing a company for up to 15 years, and confiscation orders. Under article L.267-LPF, directors who deliberately caused the tax deficiency are jointly and severally liable for the tax, penalties, and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing contracts or a chain of legal steps with no economic substance whose sole purpose is to obtain a tax benefit, e.g., interposing a shell entity in a low-tax jurisdiction to invoice the French SAS for software licences or to hold IP royalties without any employees or business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation under article L.64-LPF with a penalty of 80% of the avoided tax (or 40% where the abuse was not concealed); the case may be submitted to the Comité de l'abus de droit fiscal; loss of treaty protection and full reassessment of profits, plus interest at 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or ordered the sham arrangements are personally pursued for the 80% penalty under the 'manoeuvres frauduleuses' doctrine; in insolvency proceedings, creditors and administrators may seek 'comblement de passif' against directors for management acts contrary to the company interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the French SAS non-arm's length fees for group services (e.g., AI model licences, cloud infrastructure, R&D recharge) so that French taxable profit is artificially depressed; failure to produce the Local File / Master File within the statutory response time (30 days) upon DGFiP request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1735 ter-CGI: 5% penalty on the gross amount of undocumented cross-border intra-group transactions, added to the reassessed tax, the 40% surcharge for lack of good faith, and late-payment interest; adjustment may extend to the entire foreign group's French taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed the pricing policy are subject to personal assessment for the penalties; tax inspection reports identifying 'manoeuvres frauduleuses' allow the administration to seize assets and initiate criminal proceedings for fiscal fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the French SAS as a mere mailbox or conduit: no employees or payroll in France, no premises, no board activity, no French-based decisions for the AI video SaaS, combined with IP held offshore in a zero-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the OECD MLI / Principal Purpose Test (PPT); reclassification of the SAS under article 165 bis-CGI; application of domestic withholding on deemed distributions at 25% and on royalties at 33.33%; 80% penalty for abuse of law; potential forced liquidation of the entity by the registrar for absence of genuine activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face a personal obligation to prove the reality of the corporate seat; misrepresentation of registered office or statutory seat is a criminal offence under article L.236-3 of the French Commercial Code carrying 2 years' imprisonment and EUR 30,000 fine; directors may also be banned from managing and be ordered to restore the corporate tax paid by third parties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting or channelling funds known or suspected to derive from tax evasion or fraud, using the payment rails (Stripe, Paddle) to receive proceeds from illicit transactions, or failing to cooperate with asset-freezing measures (gel des avoirs) when the entity is flagged by Tracfin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 324-1 of the French Criminal Code: money laundering is punishable by 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 375,000; aggravated laundering (habitual, or using one's professional activity) carries 10 years' imprisonment and EUR 750,000 fine; the entity itself may be sentenced to a corporate fine of up to EUR 375,000 and dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives are presumed authors of laundering committed for the benefit of the entity; senior managers may be subjected to a crypto-asset and bank freeze, a professional interdiction, a travel ban, and confiscation of corporate property; compliance failures by the entity do not shield directors who personally approved the suspicious transactions.
